source.anchor_kjv: And it came to pass, as he went to Jerusalem, that he passed through the midst of Samaria and Galilee. And as he entered into a certain village, there met him ten men that were lepers, which stood afar off: And they lifted up their voices, and said, Jesus, Master, have mercy on us. And when he saw them, he said unto them, Go shew yourselves unto the priests. And it came to pass, that, as they went, they were cleansed. And one of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, and with a loud voice glorified God, And fell down on his face at his feet, giving him thanks: and he was a Samaritan. And Jesus answering said, Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine? There are not found that returned to give glory to God, save this stranger. And he said unto him, Arise, go thy way: thy faith hath made thee whole.
source.hook_line: Jesus told ten men with leprosy to go — before a single one of them was healed.
source.spoken_script: Jesus told ten men with leprosy to go — before a single one of them was healed. They were cleansed on the road. Only one of them came back. They'd stood at a distance, as their disease required, and cried out, "Jesus, Master, have mercy on us." He told them, "Go shew yourselves unto the priests." They obeyed before they could see any difference. "And it came to pass, that, as they went, they were cleansed." Nine kept going. One turned back, "and with a loud voice glorified God, and fell down on his face at his feet, giving him thanks: and he was a Samaritan." Jesus asked it out loud, naming exactly what nine men had skipped: "Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine? There are not found that returned to give glory to God, save this stranger." To the one still on his face, he said, "Arise, go thy way: thy faith hath made thee whole." Nine had exactly what they'd asked for, and kept walking. One turned back to him. Luke calls it thanks. Jesus calls it faith. That question didn't end with the nine. Go back and find him — at his feet, not on the road.

Luke 17:11-19: ten men with leprosy stood at a distance and cried out, "Jesus, Master, have mercy on us." Jesus told them to go show themselves to the priests, before any of them could see a difference in their skin. "And it came to pass, that, as they went, they were cleansed."

Nine kept walking toward the life they had just gotten back. One turned around. He fell at Jesus's feet, giving thanks, and he was a Samaritan, an outsider even among outsiders.

Jesus named the gap out loud: "Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine?"

Then, to the one still on the ground: "Arise, go thy way: thy faith hath made thee whole."

Ten received the same miracle. Only one received Jesus himself. Which one are you today: the nine walking on, or the one turning back?

redteam:
VERDICT: REVISE

- youtube_short + youtube_long: the mid-verse fragment is presented as if it were a stand-alone KJV sentence. The real text (Luke 17:17) is "Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine?" — a single continuous question. Both descriptions isolate only "but where are the nine?", recapitalize it to "But where are the nine?", and quote it alone as though that were the whole verse. This is not a wording change (the automated verbatim gate will pass it, since it's still the real words), but it misrepresents the SHAPE of what Jesus actually said — he asked one compound question ("were there not ten cleansed... where are the nine"), not two. Fix: quote the full clause, "Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine?", in both descriptions instead of the truncated/recapitalized half-quote.
- Everything else holds up: titles are hooky but true to the text (no invented urgency, no "shocking"/"secret" framing), every full-sentence quote checked word-for-word against the given KJV text is verbatim, doctrine is sound (Samaritan-as-outsider is the text's own point, not an added spin), CTA is grace-anchored (no fear/gain-loss language), and TikTok/Instagram read punchy with the hook in the first line while YouTube/Facebook carry the fuller narrative. No platform-mismatch or generic/templated title found.
